disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's detached per-workflow daemon — spawned by daemon-registry, owning its own HTTP control surface, lockfile, session and claim loop — is replaced by a FOREGROUND `cli worker <workflow-id> --pool-index <positive-int> [--drain]` process. Control moves off HTTP onto the one idempotent actor-stamped command family plus the authority's own claim leases. Each worker start owns a durable process record under .tracker-rebuild/locks/workers; D181 strictly aggregates those records into one restore-safety observation while identity collision remains the authority lease's job. There is no per-daemon stdout log file: a worker's events reach the operator only through the ONE projection.

disposition.reason: The rebuild CLI covers help/phase/dashboard/worker/explain/ocr/storage (src/core/runtime-composition.ts) and the operator surface is the dashboard BFF, not the CLI. Legacy's per-workflow subcommands and system probes close one at a time as each workflow migrates, and doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory requires behavioural CLI fixtures plus help output for the whole family before cutover.

2i-F (D175) landed the phone capture surface (src/dashboard/phone/) and the operator's QR start (src/dashboard/surfaces/capture-start.tsx). The operator-side photo review legacy carries — CapturePhotoTile, CapturePhotoLightbox and the capture modal — is NOT built: the run-detail `captures` section lists artifact refs but nothing serves artifact BYTES. It is therefore blocked on the same artifact route legacy-route-files owns, and closes with it.

Both views are dev-only scaffolding: legacy App.tsx reaches them solely through a `?view=` gate and marks them TEMPORARY in source with an explicit removal instruction. `dev/rebuild-demo/` was a SYNTHETIC PREVIEW OF THIS REPO's surfaces and was consumed as their port source — the provenance headers on src/dashboard/surfaces/*.tsx name legacy hr-automation@793abe1f8265f3213ffe8a80d6cfd9860a32a1dc's rebuild-demo files — so it cannot exist in the rebuild by construction. `UiGallery`'s job, seeing every primitive in both themes, is held by src/dashboard/ds/ plus the frozen `npm run test:parity` corpus, which asserts rather than rewrites. Retirement is a decision about the TARGET only: nothing here authorizes deleting the legacy source, which stays the D89 rollback asset.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's thirty bespoke fetch/SSE hooks are replaced by ONE typed transport plus a query/command client (src/dashboard/client/) and three resource hooks over the ONE projection (src/dashboard/state/). The per-endpoint polling hooks — useDaemons, useQueueDepth, useLogs, useRunEvents, useSessions, useRosters, useSharePointStatus and the rest — have no counterpart by design: their facts arrive on the single resumable SSE topic, so a second fetch path cannot disagree with the projection it is meant to describe.

disposition.reason: 1i-spine landed the Log Panel parity surface (src/dashboard/surfaces/log-panel.tsx) and 2g/2i added its receipt, failure, trust and advisory sections. Three parts remain unbuilt and each waits on a consumer that arrives with a workflow: the run screenshot gallery (ScreenshotsPanel/ScreenshotCard/ScreenshotLightbox), which needs the artifact-bytes route legacy-route-files still owns; the xlsx ExportMenu (legacy-export-export-excel); and the Review and People tabs, which render an explicit `not served yet` placeholder until an OCR/roster workflow migrates.

The top bar, date/month navigation, history controls, the D138 notification bell, the shortcuts legend and the workflow rail landed across 1i-spine/2g/2i (src/dashboard/surfaces/top-bar.tsx, shortcuts.tsx, shell.tsx). SearchBar and SearchResults are NOT built — there is no cross-run search endpoint at all — so this family closes with legacy-route-search, as the migrations produce the run corpus a search surface must be shaped by.

No oath-upload UI exists in the rebuild. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory absorbs oath-upload's special routes and surfaces into the descriptor's start surface and the standard commands at that workflow's own migration, which is order 7 (see legacy-workflow-oath-upload).

No OCR review/approve UI exists. 2h landed the one extraction gate and its CLI (`cli ocr forms|instruction|admit|stack`), but the run-detail Review and People tabs render an explicit `not served yet` placeholder (src/dashboard/surfaces/log-panel.tsx). Doc 03c §Recommended migration order states outright that the OCR review UI lands WITH the OCR workflow at orders 3-4, as an expanded-page-to-extracted-text pair.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's single OverviewPanel is split along the line the rebuild's projection already draws. The per-workflow counts are 1i-spine's Workflow Panel counts — the workflow rail plus the status filters in shell.tsx — and the range totals it also carried are D180's Activity report (src/dashboard/surfaces/activity.tsx), which is computed INSIDE run-queue-projection.ts so a second summation path cannot disagree with the day it summarises.

Run detail is an INLINE panel in the main column rather than a modal (ref frontend-backend-integration s3.3), with run identity in src/dashboard/surfaces/run-identity.tsx; the modal shape is reserved for run START (run-start.tsx, run-start-kit.tsx). SharePointDownloadButton and the OnBase form-type picker are workflow affordances rather than shell, so they land with legacy-workflow-sharepoint-download and legacy-workflow-onbase.

disposition.reason: 2i-D (D169) landed the read-only Storage section — the bootstrap health summary plus the full byte-re-verified doctor — and the SERVER owns the section list, so a served section this build cannot render says so by name. D169 records editable settings as a DEFERRED COMMAND FAMILY: `settings`/`apply-settings` is in the command union but src/dashboard/surfaces/settings.tsx states outright that nothing there pretends to save. The editable fields, the AI-assist section and the credentials reference panel therefore close with roadmap §Phases at a glance row 3's explicit non-workflow capability closure; the operator loses legacy's settings dialog at cutover, so this is a cutover-parity item rather than a workflow-coupled one.

disposition.differencesAccepted: The shared component grab-bag is folded into the design-system barrel (src/dashboard/ds/) plus ConfirmCommandDialog in surfaces/actions.tsx, so every primitive has one owner and one token source instead of a per-consumer copy. MediaLightbox and PdfPagePreview are absent because BOTH of their consumers are absent — the run screenshot gallery (legacy-dashboard-log-panel) and the OCR review pane (legacy-dashboard-ocr) — and a viewer primitive with no consumer is not a capability.

The drawer's worker/browser/workflow cards are 1i-spine's Session Panel (SessionPanel and WorkerCard in shell.tsx). The daemon stdout console has no counterpart BY CONSTRUCTION: legacy daemons were detached processes tee'd to .tracker/daemons/<workflow>-<ISO>.log, whereas a rebuild worker is a foreground process whose events reach the operator only through the ONE projection's spans and notes, so there is no second log stream to drawer.

The vendored shadcn primitives are re-authored over the rebuild's own tokens (src/dashboard/ds/tokens.ts, tokens.css, theme.ts) and exported from ONE barrel, which is what makes the tailwind-palette ratchet enforceable. `calendar` is hand-built inside top-bar.tsx against the day model rather than vendored, so the month grid and the projection agree on what a day is. `resizable` and `scroll-area` are not ported: no rebuild surface uses either.

disposition.reason: 2i-G (D176/D177) landed the READ-ONLY Workflow Explorer and the UI-catalog surface, both read-only STRUCTURALLY — no command endpoint, no command client, no non-GET request. Ref operator-trust s5.3's Phase B is DEFERRED OUT OF PHASE 2 by D186 on D79a's own argument: an editor exists to avoid a code change per tweak across MANY workflows, and this tree has one production workflow plus a one-node transaction proof, so building it now would fix its closed policy union against a sample of one. D186 names the trigger — the SECOND production workflow whose presentation, notification preference or allowlisted policy value an operator wants to change without a code change — and reassigns the criterion to the migration that first needs it, which is this milestone.

No operator xlsx export exists. src/infra/artifacts/xlsx-retention-sink.ts is a stable-keyed DURABILITY sink whose four-column layout is deliberately not a display layout, and D164 leaves it NOT composed in production because no descriptor declares a projection yet. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory requires behavioural CLI fixtures and help output for the export family before cutover.

No i9-check tracker export exists. src/infra/artifacts/xlsx-retention-sink.ts states in its own header that the i9-check operator COLUMN LAYOUT belongs to that workflow's migration; the sink only guarantees retry-safe stable-keyed materialization. This closes at order 5 with legacy-workflow-i9-check.

No generic spreadsheet exporter exists. read-excel-file is used for INGEST only (src/stores/common/spreadsheet-grid.ts, src/stores/extraction/tasks/extract-spreadsheet.ts) and write-excel-file only inside the uncomposed retention sink. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory requires behavioural CLI fixtures and help output for the export family before cutover.

POST /api/v1/runs/:runId/advisory serves failure triage (D178) and the bootstrap reports ai-advisory availability for THIS process. `sanity`, `selector` and `summarize` have no producer: D178 records all three as remaining without a producer and without a surface arm, and AdvisorySurfaceIdSchema is a closed two-value enum, so each is a declared schema change plus a redaction declaration rather than wiring. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory calls these adapters OPTIONAL with the deterministic paths primary, so closure here is a build-or-retire decision at the plan's explicit non-workflow capability closure.

GET /api/v1/bootstrap, GET /api/v1/dashboard and GET /api/v1/runs/:runId (plus its section route) serve legacy's workflows, workflow-definitions, preflight, dates, entries, runs, logs and entry-data. `rosters` has no served equivalent: the run-detail People section is typed-absent until a roster-bearing workflow migrates, which is order 3 at the earliest.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's fourteen ad-hoc capture handlers are replaced by a CLOSED, token-scoped route union: two operator endpoints plus the nine phone routes declared once in src/domain/capture-surface.ts (CAPTURE_PHONE_ROUTES) behind a host-scoped gate, so a newly added route is externally unavailable until it is explicitly reviewed. The phone PAGE bytes are not served by a route — /capture.html is allow-listed by the gate but delivered by the Vite build — which is legacy-route-static's open item, and legacy's /capture-assets/heic2any.min.js has no counterpart because the rebuild bundles the phone app rather than side-loading a script.

Legacy's dedicated POST /api/daemon/stop is replaced by the ONE idempotent actor-stamped command endpoint (POST /api/v1/commands) carrying the `worker-browser` family's stop-worker type, so every product mutation is validated by the same authority-transactional kernel instead of by a per-action route with its own ad-hoc checks.

disposition.reason: There is no per-INSTANCE stop. The command union's stop-worker addresses a worker by workflow scope, not by a spawned daemon instance id, because a rebuild worker is a foreground process holding a durable claim lease and a per-role process lock (D181) rather than a supervised detached daemon. Naming an instance would need a supervisor the rebuild does not have, and whether one is wanted is decided by how multi-worker operation actually behaves once real workflows run — so it closes with them, not ahead of them.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Enqueue is TWO steps, not one: POST /api/v1/start-plans mints a confirmable plan that retains the exact raw JSON ingress beside the schema-bound canonical snapshot and binds both schema hashes plus the canonical digest (D109), and POST /api/v1/commands then consumes that plan under the `start` family inside its own authority transaction (D113). A single fire-and-forget enqueue cannot bind the confirmation revision the terminal authority later requires.

This legacy module registers no route: it assembles the dashboard row payload for the entries SSE topic inside the route layer, and caches cross-workflow counts beside it. The rebuild builds every row and every total INSIDE the one projection (D81, and D180 for the range aggregates), so there is no second assembly path and no separate count cache that could disagree with the day it summarises.

disposition.reason: There is NO artifact-bytes endpoint. ArtifactRefWireSchema describes artifacts and the run-detail `captures` section lists them, but nothing serves their bytes; the only byte-serving route today is the phone's own GET /api/v1/capture/phone/photos/:photoId/bytes. Every real consumer — downloaded CRM/SharePoint documents, OnBase uploads, OCR page images — arrives with a phase-3 workflow, so this closes there rather than in 2i.

No oath-upload endpoints exist. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory absorbs oath-upload's special routes into the descriptor start surface and the standard commands at that workflow's migration, which is order 7 (see legacy-workflow-oath-upload).

src/server/ocr/compose.ts serves the ONE extraction gate through `cli ocr` (D151/D158) but is not routed: there are no /api/v1/ocr/* endpoints. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory puts the OCR review/approve/retry/research/discard routes at orders 3-4, native to the OCR workflow rather than ported as routes.

POST /api/v1/commands covers plan/spawn/stop/pause/resume-worker, refresh/reopen-browser and the run family (retry, cancel, bump, hide), and queue depth is `statusCounts` on GET /api/v1/dashboard. NOT built: browser kill/focus/check/screenshot/auto-recovery, worker drain over the wire (it exists only as the CLI's --drain flag), and every bulk cancel/retry/delete. Every one of those is a fact about operating MANY runs at once, and the rebuild has two workflows and no run corpus, so their consumer arrives with the migrations — which is also where a bulk affordance can be proved against real volume rather than a fixture.

No /api/screenshots, no /screenshots/:filename and no /api/prep/pdf-page. Run screenshots are produced by real runs of the workflows that take them, and serving their bytes needs the same artifact route legacy-route-files still owns, so this closes with those migrations.

There is no /api/search. Failure detail is served per run at GET /api/v1/runs/:runId/failure, and legacy's selector-warnings are subsumed by GET /api/v1/ui-catalog's stale-artifact refusal (D177), which fails loud with the generator's own remediation rather than reporting a warning. The cross-run search over runs, entries and failure fingerprints is NOT built: its consumer is a corpus of runs, and the rebuild has produced two, so shaping a search surface now would fix its ranking and its facets against nothing. It closes as the migrations produce the corpus.

GET /api/v1/bootstrap serves `settingsSections` (storage only) and GET /api/v1/storage/doctor serves the read-only doctor. The write path exists in the command union as `settings`/`apply-settings` but no surface issues it, and there is no delete or recover equivalent — D169's deferred-command-family record, from the server side. Closes with legacy-dashboard-settings under roadmap §Phases at a glance row 3's non-workflow capability closure.

No sharepoint endpoints exist. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory absorbs the workflow-special routes into the descriptor start surface and the standard commands at that workflow's migration, which is order 2 (see legacy-workflow-sharepoint-download).

The production BFF serves NO frontend bytes: src/server/dashboard/http-server.ts has no static handler, api.ts 404s everything unrouted through app.notFound, and the only dist/dashboard static servers in the tree are test-only (tests/parity/helpers/). This is more than a convenience gap — api.ts allow-lists /capture.html for the phone host gate, but nothing in production serves it, so the phone capture page has NO delivery path from the BFF. Serving the built bundle is base-integration work, which was 2j's own scope; 2j closed (D181-D186) without it, so it moves to roadmap §Phases at a glance row 3's explicit non-workflow capability closure. It is a HARD cutover blocker, not a nicety: cutover flips the operator onto this runtime, and a runtime that cannot deliver its own frontend has no operator surface at all.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's /api/task-dependencies computed a dependency graph inside the route. The rebuild derives task, contract, delegation and scenario facts from the composition root plus each descriptor's factory-sealed projections and the fingerprinted build manifest at GET /api/v1/explorer (D176) — no literal node list, no per-workflow switch — so there is no second answer that could disagree with the descriptor, and a source link that does not resolve reports `unresolved` with the path it tried instead of interpolating a plausible one.

disposition.reason: GET /api/v1/explorer serves the read-only projection (D176) and api.ts records that Phase A has no draft, no apply and no compile. The POST/DELETE design half is ref operator-trust s5.3/s5.4's Phase B, DEFERRED OUT OF PHASE 2 by D186 and reassigned to the migration that first needs it. Legacy's /api/data-bank half belongs to legacy-tool-workflow-design-build-data-bank.

Presentation facts are baked into GET /api/v1/bootstrap (workflowCategories) and GET /api/v1/explorer, but the presentation OVERRIDE family — read, preview, write and delete against a strict versioned atomic file — is ref operator-trust s5.4's apply protocol, DEFERRED OUT OF PHASE 2 by D186 and reassigned to the migration that first needs it. D186 leaves the protocol itself unchanged: strict versioned override, temp+fsync+atomic-replace, stale-base refusal, code-change brief for everything else.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's address service bundled parsing, cleanup and an LLM fallback behind one call. The rebuild splits them: deterministic canonical rules in src/domain/normalization/ (contact-rules, street-safety, geocode), two admitted geocode providers under D112 budget admission (geocode.census and geocode.nominatim in src/infra/providers/geocode-adapters.ts), and an optional advisory arm that is deliberately NARROWER than legacy's — only fields whose canonical transform is `allow` are asked about, so `relationship`, the one field the legacy LLM fallback existed for, stays `ambiguous` for the operator (D178). Contact-normalization parity against a real consumer is proved at OCR order 3.

disposition.reason: 2i-G (D178) landed the zero-authority advisory edge — per-leaf declared redaction, the answer schema travelling with the question, typed exhaustion, and a durable footprint that is only the D112 admission row — with exactly TWO declared surfaces: failure-triage and contact-normalization. Legacy's run summary, record sanity check and selector suggestion have no producer and no surface arm (D178), and AdvisorySurfaceIdSchema is closed. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory calls these adapters OPTIONAL with deterministic explain/rules/catalog primary, so this closes as a build-or-retire decision at non-workflow capability closure.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's matching service carried hardcoded header matchers beside its identity comparison. The rebuild's identity matching is pure Clock-free domain logic (levenshtein, name-match, match-confidence, roster-match) over the canonical field registry, header discovery is owned by intake (src/domain/intake/header-discovery.ts) with generic duplicate-safe column mapping, and the roster read sits behind a store contract (src/stores/roster/tasks/match-spreadsheet.ts). Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory's 'no hardcoded header matcher survives' therefore holds structurally; each real consumer closes during orders 3-9.

disposition.reason: 1b did not build a schema-export codegen and nothing in the rebuild emits schemas to disk: the only JSON-Schema projection is in-process (z.toJSONSchema, consumed by the advisory instruction) and is never written. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory requires the codegen family to carry behavioural CLI fixtures and help output before cutover, so this moves to the plan's explicit non-workflow capability closure rather than sitting on a closed Phase-1 milestone.

A NAMED supported diagnostic in legacy — src/scripts/CLAUDE.md documents map/test/explore as the selector-discovery and isolation path — so doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory's 'port only if a named supported diagnostic remains' applies rather than retirement. The rebuild covers selector discovery with `npm run selector:search` plus the pre-authorized playwright-cli loop, and login with scripts/live-browser-login-smoke.ts, but the Kronos timecard isolation run has no counterpart. Old Kronos closes at order 2 and New Kronos at order 8.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's main-module helper answered 'was this module executed directly'. `isDirectExecution(moduleUrl)` in scripts/scope-files.ts answers the same question for the one consumer that has it (scripts/suite-size.ts). src/ has no direct-execution branch at all, because every runtime entry point is src/cli.ts and every composition root is invoked from there rather than guessing whether it was imported.

disposition.reason: There is no `storage clean`. The retention machinery exists — createDiagnosticRetentionSweep in src/services/trust/diagnostic-retention.ts, plus the bundle purge in the authority database, which deliberately leaves content-addressed bytes alone and reports unreferenced artifact ids instead of deleting them — but NO command invokes it and it is referenced only from tests. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory requires behavioural CLI fixtures and help output for the maintenance family before cutover.

No VACUUM or compaction path exists anywhere in src/infra/sqlite/; `storage doctor` reports pending durable work and backup health but never compacts. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory requires behavioural CLI fixtures and help output for the maintenance family before cutover.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Enrollment moved out of the CLI into the Duo Autopilot extension's own options page (`Set up a credential` then `Enroll`, documented in duo-autopilot/README.md), which is where the WebAuthn ceremony can actually run. The rebuild runtime only CONSUMES the stored credential: src/domain/secrets.ts is its single reader and assertDuoAutopilotReady in src/infra/browser/browser-session-factory.ts refuses a session when it is missing rather than falling through to a manual Duo wait. A brand-new credential enrollment stays the one step Duo Autopilot cannot do unattended.

disposition.reason: Operator ruling 2026-08-18 (ref operator-trust §4.4): no AI feature — D192's deferral condition ('renders beside the order-8 ALWAYS-GATE identity approval') was met DETERMINISTICALLY by the ref write-safety §14.2 gate packet's server-computed comparisons array, which puts the disconfirming Kuali-beside-UCPath evidence in exactly the slot the AI prose was reserved for. The deterministic comparison IS the sanity check. AdvisorySurfaceIdSchema stays closed at its D178 two-value shape; no surface arm is ever added. Reopening requires a fresh decision, not a build.

D192 (operator, 2026-08-12): retired as an OPERATOR surface. An operator-facing LLM selector suggestion is an unverified selector reaching a live driver — the exact fail-loud, no-unverified-fallback pattern this repo bans — so it never becomes a runtime surface. The DETERMINISTIC catalog half stays primary and closed (`npm run selector:search`, see legacy-tool-selectors-search); selector discovery and repair remain the dev-time live-verification loop root `CLAUDE.md`'s 'Live verification' section pre-authorizes. AdvisorySurfaceIdSchema stays closed at its D178 two-value shape; no surface arm is added.

No first-run setup script and no `npm run setup` exists; a fresh checkout is configured by copying .env.example and letting src/domain/config/resolve.ts apply env > settings.json > default. Doc 03c §Non-workflow capability closure inventory groups setup with the CLI/maintenance family that needs behavioural fixtures and help output before cutover.

D192 (operator, 2026-08-12): retired rather than built. `RunEvidenceReceipt` (D141/D144) is already the run's structured, byte-reproducible, per-field-redaction-declared summary, derived from authority and served by both `cli explain run <traceId|runId>` and the run-detail receipt section — an LLM digest over the same facts would duplicate it and reintroduce paraphrase risk on the exact surface D141 built to eliminate. AdvisorySurfaceIdSchema stays closed at its D178 two-value shape; no surface arm is added.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy triage was an ops SCRIPT that read a run and prompted a model. The rebuild's failure triage is a dashboard POST behind an explicit button — never a run-detail section, which would spend a provider budget every time an operator opened a failed run — assembled from the failure record's leaves each through the one redactValue under a declared (classification, transform) pair, admitted under D112 against the SUBJECT run, and rendered with provider/model/template/digest plus the standing 'not evidence, changes nothing' sentence. `summary` and `causeChain.summary` are sensitive-hr/drop because they are error.message verbatim. There is no CLI path.

The legacy tool scraped TypeScript property paths out of src/systems/<sys>/selectors.ts by AST and emitted SELECTORS.md. The rebuild generates generated/ui-catalog.json plus per-system UI-CATALOG.md from the server-only semantic registry, so catalog identity is a stable semantic id rather than a source property path (ref operator-trust s1.1/s1.3) and private locator/state/read recipes are omitted.

The legacy CLI searched selector source plus LESSONS markdown. The rebuild resolves operator language against the recipe-free generated catalog only, fails loud on a stale catalog, and fails loud on zero matches instead of printing an empty result. Lesson search returns with the 2i knowledge surfaces.

The legacy weighted title/tag/body scorer over indexed markdown sections is not ported. Ranking now runs over the closed catalog projection's id/label/searchTerms, which are curated vocabulary rather than scraped prose, so substring stemming heuristics are unnecessary; a search-term collision fails catalog generation instead of being resolved by score.
